title: VPN Not Connecting from Home
problem: Employees cannot connect to the company VPN or the connection drops while working remotely.
steps: Check whether normal websites open on your home internet connection.
Close and reopen the VPN application.
Confirm that the VPN client is updated to the company-approved version.
Try connecting again. If the problem continues, contact the IT helpdesk.

title: Forgotten Password or Account Locked
problem: An employee forgot their password or cannot sign in because the account is locked.
steps: Open the company's approved password-reset page.
Use the registered verification method to complete the reset.
Wait five minutes before trying the new password.
If the account remains locked, raise an IT ticket. Never share a password or OTP.

title: Microsoft Teams App Running Slowly on Mac
problem: The Teams desktop application uses high CPU or heats up a Mac laptop.
steps: Quit Teams completely and reopen it.
Install the latest approved Teams version and macOS updates.
Close other resource-intensive applications and try again.
If the issue continues, use the browser version temporarily and report the desktop app problem to IT.

title: Office Wi-Fi Connection Problems
problem: An employee's laptop cannot connect to the office Wi-Fi network.
steps: Check that Wi-Fi is enabled and airplane mode is turned off.
Select the correct corporate Wi-Fi network.
Disconnect and reconnect to the network.
If other devices also cannot connect, report a possible office network outage.

title: Outlook Is Not Receiving Email
problem: New emails are not appearing in the Outlook desktop application.
steps: Check the internet connection and whether Outlook is in offline mode.
Open Outlook on the web to check whether messages arrive there.
Restart the desktop application and check its sync status.
If email works on the web but not on desktop, raise an application support ticket.

title: Laptop Overheating or Fan Running Constantly
problem: An employee reports excessive heat or continuous fan noise from a laptop.
steps: Place the laptop on a flat, ventilated surface.
Close unused applications and check which processes use the most CPU.
Restart the laptop and install approved system updates.
If it becomes dangerously hot, smells unusual, or the battery swells, stop using it and contact IT immediately.
